answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a crystal-clear identity bond: each agent locks one time-locked deposit per identity before trading. A nebula of peer attestations checks that every identity has distinct work history and hardware proof; duplicates or forged credentials trigger slashing of the bond. An attacker's cost rises linearly, since each fake identity needs its own deposit, while honest agents reclaim theirs after a short withdrawal delay. Auditors can flag fraud during the delay, so an umber swarm of shadow identities costs more than it can ever earn.
